value.text: One standing house rule for our playlist tool, meant for every feature we add: whenever an input object carries a key that the current task does not recognize, reject it before any other check and name the unrecognized key that comes first in alphabetical order, formatted exactly as: unexpected key '<name>'. Everything else about a feature, including its recognized keys, validation order, identifier scheme, success shape, and exact rejection wording, is established by that feature's own task description rather than by any further shared convention.

Locked in: a single shared rule for every feature. Any unrecognized key is rejected before any other check, naming the alphabetically first unrecognized key as unexpected key '<name>'. Each task description fully specifies its own recognized keys, validation order, identifiers, outputs, and exact messages.

Implement normalize_tracklist(payload) in playlist_prep.py on top of parse_track and format_clock. Exactly this behavior: if payload is not an object, return {"ok": false, "error": "payload must be an object with a 'tracks' list"}. Recognized top-level keys are only "tracks" and "allow_duplicates"; any other key follows the standing house rule before anything else. If "tracks" is absent or not a list, return the same payload error as above. If "allow_duplicates" is present and is not a boolean, return {"ok": false, "error": "'allow_duplicates' must be a boolean when present"}; when absent it counts as false. Next validate each entry in list order with parse_track and, at the first failure, return {"ok": false, "error": "track <n>: <reason>"} where <n> is the 1-based index and <reason> is parse_track's error. Only after every entry validates, apply duplicate handling: two tracks are duplicates when artist and title match ignoring letter case. Unless allow_duplicates is true, stop at the first repeat and return {"ok": false, "error": "duplicate track <n>"} naming the 1-based position of the LATER occurrence; if allow_duplicates is true, keep every validated track in input order. On success return ok true, count, total_seconds (sum of seconds of every kept track), total_clock from format_clock(total_seconds), and tracks: the kept tracks in input order, each as {"id", "title", "artist", "seconds", "explicit", "clock"} where id is assigned in processing order as T01, T02, and so on, zero-padded to at least two digits, and clock is format_clock(track seconds). An empty list is a valid success with count 0. Do not change parse_track, format_clock, or the remaining stubs.

Implement sequence_playlist(payload) in playlist_prep.py, calling normalize_tracklist. Exact behavior: recognized top-level keys are only "tracks", "order", "allow_duplicates"; any other key follows the standing house rule before any other check. A non-object payload is handed to normalize_tracklist as-is and its result returned. "order" is optional and defaults to "artist"; a present value other than "artist" or "duration" returns {"ok": false, "error": "'order' must be 'artist' or 'duration'"}. Call normalize_tracklist with exactly the input's tracks and, when present, allow_duplicates; if it returns ok false, return that result unchanged. On success, take the normalized track objects (keep all fields, ids unchanged) and order them: "artist" sorts ascending by artist ignoring letter case; "duration" sorts ascending by seconds; per the standing rule tracks equal under the chosen key keep their original relative order. Return {"ok": true, "order": <effective order>, "count": <count from normalization>, "total_seconds": <total from normalization>, "tracks": <ordered tracks>}. Do not redefine or patch normalize_tracklist, parse_track, or format_clock.

Implement build_manifest(payload) in playlist_prep.py on top of sequence_playlist. Exact behavior: recognized top-level keys are only "tracks", "order", "allow_duplicates", "title", "gap_seconds"; any other key follows the standing house rule before any other check. A non-object payload is handed to sequence_playlist as-is and its result returned. "title" is required: if absent return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' is required"}; if not a string return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' must be a string"}; clean it by stripping outer whitespace and collapsing each internal whitespace run to one space, and if blank return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' must not be blank"}; the cleaned title is echoed in the output. "gap_seconds" is optional, default 2: present but not an integer (true and false do not count) returns {"ok": false, "error": "'gap_seconds' must be an integer"}; a negative value returns {"ok": false, "error": "'gap_seconds' must not be negative"}. Then call sequence_playlist with exactly tracks, order (when present) and allow_duplicates (when present); an ok-false result is returned unchanged. Build entries from the sequenced tracks: for the artist ordering only, apply the current manifest rule — tracks by the same artist (ignoring case) are listed longest first, and equal lengths keep the sequenced relative order; the duration ordering is used exactly as sequenced. Each entry is {"position": 1-based, "id", "title", "artist", "seconds", "clock", "start", "start_clock", "explicit"} where "start" is the sum of the durations of all earlier entries plus gap_seconds once per boundary before it (first entry starts at 0) and "start_clock" is format_clock(start). Return {"ok": true, "title": <cleaned>, "order": <effective order>, "count", "gap_seconds", "total_seconds": durations plus gap_seconds*(count-1), or 0 when empty, "total_clock": format_clock(total_seconds), "entries"}. Do not redefine or patch the earlier functions.
